progression.summary: U1 identity and personal information -> U2 origins -> U3 routines -> U4 preferences -> U5 family -> U6 jobs -> U7 food and quantifiers -> U8 possessions -> U9 directions -> U10 places -> U11 comparisons -> U12 superlatives -> U13 present progressive -> U14 past simple -> U15 used to -> U16 past progressive -> U17 going to -> U18 future arrangements.
progression.assessment: The grammar progression is broadly coherent. Malformed vocabulary blocks in U5, U6, U7, U10, U11, U12, and U14, plus the U6 fragmented instruction, U11 topic carryover, U16 table/task mismatch, and U18 time-horizon mismatch weaken scaffolding and learner clarity.

progression: U19–20 move from close-future simple present to will predictions; U21–24 progress through present perfect, modals, indefinite pronouns, and relative clauses; U25–28 move from adjective meanings through zero/first/second conditionals; U29–32 move from gerunds and infinitives through description, adverbial clauses, and requests; U33–37 move through customs, time, probability, advice, and preferences. Progression is broadly coherent, but malformed vocabulary blocks and local instruction contradictions interrupt scaffolding.

The sequence is coherent overall: causatives (38), phrasal and delexical verbs (39–40), past perfect, reported speech, tag questions, and passive voice (41–44), third conditional and past modals (45–46), regrets and past probability (47–48), present/future likelihood and counterfactuals (49–51), future perfect/continuous (52), mixed conditionals (53–55), and nominal phrases (56). Units 53–55 provide a clear mixed-conditional time-axis progression. Topic continuity is weaker in several reading-to-writing transitions, but that is an editorial preference rather than a confirmed language defect.
